source.title: Dynamical Isometry and a Mean Field Theory of LSTMs and GRUs
source.authors: Dar Gilboa; B. Chang; Min-Min Chen; Greg Yang; S. Schoenholz; Ed H. Chi; Jeffrey Pennington

record.file_problem: Full text is present; no material cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Tests initialization-dependent trainability in recurrent networks on long-sequence classification tasks, using training accuracy and test accuracy rather than the claim's benchmark training-error measure.
record.gate_note: Results include training-accuracy comparisons for critical versus standard initialization, and test-accuracy values on unrolled MNIST and CIFAR-10. The paper also reports Jacobian spectrum measurements and mean-field predictions; these do not directly measure training classification error. Cited findings from prior work are not extracted as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study tests initialization-dependent training of gated recurrent networks across sequence lengths. V4 concerns plain feedforward networks across layer depths; recurrent time steps do not establish that version. The other versions are also untested. Feedforward initialization results are discussed as prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: initialization schemes motivated by stable forward and backward signal propagation dramatically improve long-sequence recurrent training, with standard initialization sometimes much slower or unsuccessful. The authors also report beneficial generalization results and acknowledge unresolved choices of initialization, task-dependent propagation timescale and departures from the untied-weight assumption.
record.recipe_differences: Studies recurrent LSTM/GRU cells on long-sequence tasks, using critical versus standard initialization; does not use the claim's convolutional CIFAR training-error recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization choice and sequence length change training speed and success; the tied-weight padded-MNIST setting shows deviations from predictions under the untied-weight assumption.

fits_no_version.finding: Critical initialization matches standard initialization on short recurrent sequences, accelerates training by orders of magnitude on intermediate sequences, and enables training when standard initialization fails on longer sequences.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For peephole LSTMs, initialization chosen to stabilize signal propagation can improve training speed and success as sequence length increases.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 reports critical-model test accuracies of 98.9% on unrolled MNIST and 61.8% on unrolled CIFAR-10, alongside standard-LSTM values of 98.6% and 58.8%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Critically initialized recurrent models achieve higher reported test accuracy than the listed standard-LSTM comparators on these benchmarks; the table alone does not establish a controlled initialization-only effect.

fits_no_version.finding: Predicted propagation timescale tracks training success on padded MNIST with untied recurrent weights. Appendix D.2 reports a similar general tendency with tied weights, with deviations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization-dependent propagation timescale predicts recurrent training success under the tested conditions, with imperfect transfer from untied to tied weights.

fits_no_version.finding: Approximately dynamical-isometric initialization changes the peephole-LSTM Jacobian spectrum, whose empirical moments agree with theoretical predictions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization controls state-to-state Jacobian conditioning in the tested untied peephole LSTM.

record.problems: Most training-accuracy outcomes are figure-only without exact values or uncertainty estimates. The study notes deviations when the untied-weights assumption is violated and says tied-weight behavior is outside the analysis scope. CIFAR-10 and MNIST values in Table 2 are test accuracy, not training error.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible result rows omitted. R11 is not retained: it is an invalid GRU assignment; the Section 5.4 figure and text concern peephole LSTM.

untested.parts: Convolutional training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and size, stopping or regularization effects.
Spurious local minima and extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with feedforward depth, identity shortcuts, deep plain tanh networks and Fixup.
Initialization-dependent learning speed and trainable layer depth in plain feedforward networks; orthogonal versus Gaussian deep tanh weights; 10,000-layer convolutional training.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
Batch-normalization training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are assigned because no listed version is tested. Figure-only reporting does not invalidate the explicit qualitative training comparisons. Tied-weight and task-dependent-timescale qualifications concern the recurrent extension, not limitations demonstrated for V4.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, or the stated effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student local-minimum experiment or neuron-width comparison.
No plain-versus-residual depth comparison, shortcut ablation, or normalization comparison.

Although initialization is varied, the study tests recurrent LSTM/GRU initialization and sequence trainability, not the stated plain feedforward depth, tanh orthogonal-versus-Gaussian, or 10,000-layer convolutional claims.
No learning-rate-above-stability-limit experiment or sharpness tracking.
No batch-normalization comparison or Fixup experiment.

rows.subject: peephole LSTM
rows.operation_detail: Compared critical and standard initialization on unrolled, concatenated MNIST digits; the text reports the qualitative outcome rather than numeric accuracies.
rows.value: Critical and standard initialization perform equivalently for shorter sequences; critical initialization is faster by orders of magnitude as sequence length increases; standard initialization fails at very long sequence lengths while critical initialization succeeds.
rows.note: Qualitative comparison stated in text; no exact plotted values are given.
rows.check: The qualitative training advantage is explicitly reported, but concerns gated recurrent networks rather than V4's plain feedforward networks. The partial state is inappropriate for a row linked to no version. Figure 4 compares 1, 4 and 8 digits.

rows.note: Qualitative comparison stated in text; no exact plotted values are given.

rows.subject: peephole LSTM
rows.operation_detail: Measured state-to-state Jacobian squared-singular-value spectrum after 100 iterations with i.i.d. Gaussian inputs, comparing typical and approximately dynamical-isometry initialization.
rows.measure: Squared singular-value spectrum and its first two moments
rows.value: Approximate dynamical isometry produces a dramatically different spectrum; empirical averages agree well with theoretical prediction.
rows.note: The text describes a dramatic spectrum difference and good agreement; specific plotted numerical values are not given.
rows.check: This measures a recurrent Jacobian spectrum after 100 forward time steps, not 100 training iterations or learning performance. Specify untied weights. The reported spectrum difference cannot establish a listed version.

rows.note: Figure caption identifies the task curves as peephole LSTM; no GRU is reported for this task. Excluded from rows because it is not a GRU result.
